report:
PASS for the finite, unconditional and explicitly conditional assertions in the four supplied mathematical bodies, in their stated scopes. This accepts supporting arguments relative to G0/G1 and the external premises below. It does not establish the actual nonample foundations or complete P16.5.

I treated G0 as an actual-ample grant and G1 as resolved relative generation plus its one FS net. S1–S3/M1–M2 and the corresponding S–M–A–C packages remained logical antecedents throughout. Author ledgers, historical verdicts and compilation claims supplied no mathematical evidence. The two unindexed task passages record this authority; external premises have indices 0–10.

Whole159, §§2–4: the graph identity retains every b_i and the diagonal zero-row identities. Resolving the absolute value before applying the graph formula proves the contraction without introducing horizontal poles. The tangent remainder has coefficients n−j with the displayed factors. The midpoint constants n/4^(n+1) and n/8, including the exact n=1 identity, follow from the stated Green kernel. The slot-change recurrence, its quasi-triangle argument and averaging give the claimed exponents. The absolute moment estimate retains |ξ(v0)−η(v0)|V_A, including V_A=0 and the exponent-zero convention in dimension one.

The full-lattice volume calculation uses the entire original section space. Its eventual intercept, refinement invariance, concavity and raw constant law are valid. BFJ differentiation supplies the finite positive measures with coefficient b_E⟨α^n⟩·E. The negative-part trace proves coefficientwise deficient-measure domination, beyond merely controlling total mass; its missing mass is at most B/c. The Taylor proof pairs order inequalities only with two fixed nef tests. Its constants remain independent of the obstacle and refinement. The signed path stays big because the proof explicitly imposes |t|‖h‖∞<(c−B/V)/2. Both signs and the displayed linear tail error are justified.

Whole160, §§2–4: generating systems preserve the scalar at every semivaluation, so the ample embedding is literal on the original carrier. The bounded minorants use actual bundle differences and fix their parameters before selecting a tail. G1's single endpoint first identifies each model envelope; decreasing closure is not used circularly. In the flattening proof, the old reference bounds control old poles, δ is chosen below every old δ_l, the new actual ample gaps are established before section tensoring, and the positive guard remains separate from the weakened pole floor. The two compact comparison arguments produce a common lower stage. The resulting directed family is one genuine FS net with the required all-point infimum, including supported −∞ values. No cofinal sequence or countability assumption enters.

Continuous model majorants then give the stated usc obstacle envelopes. The regularized supremum is identified by the envelope inequalities at every point. For normalized compactness, the finite PL separator is applied inside the common actual ample cone: each rational divisorial coordinate of a regularized tail supremum equals its raw coordinate. Decreasing closure and ample order determination identify the limiting function. The supplied convex-ray argument also justifies the extension from rational to real divisorial scalings.

Whole160, §§5–7: the ample embedding preserves both the raw supremum and its usc regularization because it preserves all pointwise values and the topology. The negligible-to-polar theorem is applied with irreducibility, an actual ample class and EP from G0. The return to L uses the actual identity L=tΩ+E and section tensoring, producing one defining net. It asserts no finite-energy membership for that transferred pole. Under the explicitly assumed energy and contraction inputs, the pole series has energy at least −CV/7 and relative deficit m on the required pole set. Its integrability supplies a Borel null superset, hence outer nullness for arbitrary non-Borel negligible subsets.

Whole160, §§8–10 and its final zero-volume section: finite polarization retains the factors |S|^n/n! and every raw multiplicity. Its stated diagonal-convergence antecedent suffices for positivity and restricted independence; maximum convergence alone does not supply that antecedent. The blowup section counts, piecewise volume formula and erroneous quadratic-interpolation value 33/32 are correct. The numerical-zero cone consists of constants by the fixed ample coordinate bounds applied to integer multiples. Its raw equation has only the zero target and no division by volume. The nonzero nef zero-volume example on P1×P1 has a nonconstant bounded scalar and perturbation mass 2ε(1+ε), correctly demonstrating failure of uniqueness for the raw zero equation.

Whole159, all proofs following its §5 package: the bounded density and directed Radon integration arguments preserve their stated scopes. The intrinsic targets use relative costs and exclude reference poles; absolute integrability of R is not assumed. The midpoint trace injection retains the signed term (min f)(V−V_A) until after the fixed-degree trace limit. The order is fixed auxiliary model and finite majorant, then section degree, then moving model, then outer infimum. Physical functions with horizontal poles are never assigned original E1 membership.

The absolute estimates pass to genuine outputs and intrinsic finite-dual targets through bounded tests, ordered errors and the stated canonical convergence. Actual divisorial Dirac probes have finite intrinsic dual energy by the ample coordinate bounds, independently of solving their equations. Finite supporting planes extend to whole supporting planes under the package. For model near-maximizers, midpoint defects give the required absolute errors; finite divisorial planes and coordinate convergence exclude an energy jump. The limit is an actual genuine finite-energy maximizer. The original variational inequality is tested in both continuous directions, identifying its output with the target. Every solution maximizes by the whole planes, and divisorial probes separate every pair of normalized solutions. Thus uniqueness applies to every solution, including all-point equality at supported poles.

Whole201: the moving maximum is a union of systems in the same degree on the same actual A_m. The fixed global time twist generates both charts and gives nef compactifications dominated by the fixed algebraic upper class. The divisor collars and signed quadratic bounds use fixed nef tests and retain central multiplicities. The whole-system trace inequality retains (min h)(V−A_m^n). Canonical upper systems have one uniform time window even when the original majorants have no uniform sup-norm bound. The retained-volume energy squeeze identifies the maximum energy; the ordered gap and finite Hodge estimate identify its measure.

Finite nef locality follows through a common actual ample perturbation on a fixed model. General decreasing weak continuity follows by taking fixed signed secants before shrinking their increments. The ordered-tail modulus is uniform over bounded-cost outputs. In the Borel proof, wrong selection forces u_j−u_i>ε, giving the explicit error 2‖h‖∞η_j(D)/ε. The proof correctly holds the continuous ramp fixed through the output limit, then takes the majorant limit in absolute L1, and finally an ordinary ramp-width sequence at fixed measures. The strict comparison uses equal raw masses. The conditional pole-series proof gives genuine PSH-pole nullness under S–C and the specified integrability/nullness assumptions.

Whole202, §§2–4: adapted full, subspace and quotient flags give exact trace additivity. Quotient rank yields Lipschitz constant V−V_A. The restricted lattice removes T^hor and retains T^ver. The derivative difference has norm at most V−V_A and that same value on 1, forcing positivity and total variation exactly V−V_A. The V_A=0 case follows from subleading rank and requires no differentiation of a nonbig auxiliary class.

Original time-deficient collars and bounded auxiliary collars remain separate. Restricted complete systems occupy one fixed time window and global twist. Complete-base-system Fujita approximation gives their volume convergence. The full BFJ Morse inequality, applied to H and −H with one fixed nef upper class, squeezes the derivative tests after the degree limit. The ordered energy gap then gives the uniform square-root measure comparison.

Whole202, §§5–9: the physical minorants are actual original FS scalars. Their floors max(v_m,R−N) are genuine E1 functions with bounded normalized cost, and the generic errors b_m→0 are retained. Original collars and whole planes identify floor energies; both signed fixed-increment Taylor bounds identify floor outputs. At shifted canonical majorants the quotient trace is nonpositive. Auxiliary collars control the strict losing-region mass, yielding the physical auxiliary energy and measure identification with the missing-volume term retained.

Rational tensor combinations remain on the same actual A_m, and their horizontal factor is exactly Σt_iT_m=T_m. Finite rational unisolvent matrices are fixed before any moving limit. Their positive raw mixed coefficients converge, and bounded parameter continuity covers real simplex weights. Canonical majorants extend the polarization to the entire genuine E1 domain. Positivity gives the stated n^n/n! domination, hence all-test integrability and divisor nullness. Weighted decreasing continuity uses uniform ordered errors and fixed continuous collars; simultaneously decreasing tests retain V|v_k(v0)−v(v0)|. These arguments work for general product-directed nets. The finite telescoping identity passes first to bounded pairs and then, using those weighted estimates, to the full mixed energy identity.

Two harmless application clarifications should be explicit. In whole201's Strict Borel comparison proof, applying (12) to (u,v−ε) requires the same locality proof with the second auxiliary weights shifted by −ε; constant invariance alone is not the justification. I checked that extension: it preserves the actual bundle and horizontal factor, enlarges the fixed bound by ε, shifts energy by −εA_m^n, and leaves the collar, ordered-gap and ramp arguments valid. In whole202 §1, display (1) is for generically normalized potentials, as its surrounding normalization and constant-restoration text specifies. For arbitrary constants the restored estimate includes V|u(v0)−v(v0)|. Its weighted-limit proof already retains this error. Zero simplex entries are omitted, avoiding 0·(−∞).

Primary checking used independently opened statement/proof units, not the supplied reading ledgers. BJ v4: Rees/interpolation and finite detection units, Theorem 5.6/Lemma 5.7 at renderer 3996–4022, and Theorem 13.17/Lemma 13.19 at 10614–10647 with their polar, Choquet and capacity dependencies. BFJ v2: §§2–3 through Theorem A, including the complete Corollary 3.4 proof. Lazarsfeld–Mustață's published 2009 text: section asymptotics and complete-system Fujita units, including Remark 3.7. Włodarczyk: marked-resolution algorithm, principalization reduction and smooth functoriality. Vakil's retained 2011 proof unit and the cited Stacks statement/proof units cover the remaining algebraic applications. BJ's separator constant can be enlarged to a rational constant. In Vakil's openness proof the displayed box is replaced by the smaller convex-hull neighborhood; its section-on-the-complement wording means nonvanishing. These are harmless source wording corrections.

The actual Kodaira decomposition also follows from the registered algebraic inputs: restriction to a fixed very ample divisor has O(m^(n−1)) section growth, whereas big L has positive m^n growth. Thus some cleared mL−H has a nonzero section, giving L=H/m+E as an actual bundle identity. Openness permits the small ample subtraction used for pole transfer. Exceptional-divisor section invariance follows from normal extension across codimension two.

No essential extra premise remains unverified in these supporting arguments. Their conditional antecedents remain unproved on the actual nonample domain. The complete nonample energy/output/moving foundations, every simultaneously unbounded physical weighted approximation, and further nonzero zero-volume theory are not established by this PASS.

passages.statement: For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and an actual ample rational bundle Ω, each rational divisorial valuation v, including the generic trivial valuation, admits a continuous PL function ψ such that sup_K(u−ψ)=(u−ψ)(v) for every genuine Ω-psh u. Consequently, for every nonempty uniformly upper bounded such family with raw supremum S, S*(v)=S(v). BJ arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 5.6 and Lemma 5.7.

For an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, an ample class Ω having the envelope property, and a nonempty uniformly upper bounded family of genuine Ω-psh functions with raw supremum S, every subset of {S<S*}, without a Borel hypothesis, is contained in the pole set of a genuine Ω-psh function. BJ arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 13.17 and Lemma 13.19.

passages.statement: On smooth projective varieties over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, algebraic positive products preserve pseudoeffective order, are symmetric and separately homogeneous, and equal ordinary products for nef entries. On big classes they are continuous and are suprema of products of dominated nef Cartier classes on birational models. The resulting inequalities hold against fixed nef tests. BFJ arXiv:math/0608260v2, §2.

For a projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, volume is numerical, continuous, homogeneous of degree d, zero outside the big cone, and has concave d-th root on the big cone. It is C1 there, with Dvol_α(H)=d⟨α^(d−1)⟩·H. BFJ arXiv:math/0608260v2, Theorem A and §§2–3.

passages.statement: On a projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, if β≤ω is nef, ω is nef and big, and ω±H are nef, then vol(β±tH)≥β^d±dtβ^(d−1)·H−Ct² for 0≤t≤1, with C depending only on d and ω^d. BFJ arXiv:math/0608260v2, Corollary 3.4.

For an actual big rational Cartier divisor D on an integral projective d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, h0(mD)=vol(D)m^d/d!+o(m^d) along denominator-cleared positive degrees, without countability or finite generation of its section ring. Lazarsfeld–Mustață, Convex Bodies Associated to Linear Series, published 2009 text, Proposition 2.1, Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 2.3.

passages.statement: On a smooth variety over a characteristic-zero field, a coherent nonzero ideal can be principalized by finitely many blowups with smooth centers compatible with a prescribed SNC boundary, making its total transform an invertible effective SNC ideal. The construction is unchanged off the ideal's zero locus and is functorial for smooth morphisms and field extensions. Invariant ideals therefore admit equivariant principalizations. Włodarczyk, Simple Hironaka Resolution in Characteristic Zero, JAMS 18 (2005).

passages.statement: For projective varieties over the retained fields, ampleness of an actual rational bundle depends only on its numerical class; the ample cone is open and convex, its closure is the nef cone, and a nef class plus a positive ample class is ample. Vakil, Foundations of Algebraic Geometry, 27 June 2011 version, §22.3.

If p:Y→X is proper birational, Y is integral and reduced, and X is integral and normal, then p_*O_Y=O_X. Consequently H0(Y,p*B)=H0(X,B) for every actual line bundle B, and for rational bundles after denominator clearing. Stacks Project, Lemma 37.53.6, tag 0AY8, and projection formula.

If X is a projective noetherian scheme, H is an actual ample integral line bundle and F is coherent, then F⊗H^m is globally generated for every sufficiently large integer m. Stacks Project, Proposition 28.27.13, tag 01PR.
